rules.title: Rent increases barred for conversion costs (Anti-Eviction Act, conversion provision)
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Rents may still be raised to cover the cost of new services or amenities, and the bar protects all tenants regardless of senior or disabled protected-tenancy status.
rules.status_basis: Cited as existing statute in the NJ DCA landlord-tenant information publication.

requires.name: building_converted_to_condo_coop_or_fee_simple
requires.text: a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units

coverage.summary: Applies to buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple unit ownership.

rules.quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).
